title: 2014 HMMT February Guts Problem 2
statement: Let \(x_{1}, \ldots, x_{100}\) be defined so that for each \(i, x_{i}\) is a (uniformly) random integer between 1 and 6 inclusive. Find the expected number of integers in the set \(\left\{x_{1}, x_{1}+x_{2}, \ldots, x_{1}+x_{2}+\ldots+x_{100}\right\}\) that are multiples of 6 .

solutions.text: \(\boxed{\frac{50}{3}}\) Note that for any \(i\), the probability that \(x_1 + x_2 + ... + x_i\) is a multiple of 6 is \(\frac{1}{6}\) because exactly 1 value out of 6 possible values of \(x_{i}\) works. Because these 100 events are independent, the expected value is \(100 \cdot \frac{1}{6}=\frac{50}{3}\).
